etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English twenty, twenti, from Old English twēntiġ (“twenty”, literally “two tens”), from Proto-Germanic *twaintigiwiz, *twai tigiwiz, an old compound of *twain- (“two”) +‎ *-tigaz (“group of ten”), equivalent to two + -ty, or twain + -ty. Cognate with Scots twenty, tuenty (“twenty”), West Frisian tweintich (“twenty”), Dutch twintig (“twenty”), German zwanzig (“twenty”), Danish tyve.

definitions.definition: (in the plural) The numbers twenty (20) to twenty-nine (29).
(colloquial) A banknote with a denomination of 20.

quote.citation: 2020 September 1, Tom Lamont, “The butcher's shop that lasted 300 years (give or take)”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: The more a shop looks as though it trades in farthings and ha’pennies, the more tenners and twenties you can expect to hand over at the till.

quote.citation: 2012, Tom Dumont, Tony Kanal, Gwen Stefani, 0:54 from the start, in Settle Down‎[2] (music video), No Doubt (actor), Vevo:
quote.text: What's your twenty?  Where's your brain?  Checking in to check you out  Concerned about your whereabouts

definitions.definition: (UK, historical, military) An old English division of infantry.
